## What this does

Before any Round-11 acquisition fetch, the crawler identifies itself with a
contact URL on the domain SIG owns — `https://surveillancegraph.org/data-collection/`
— and that URL builds to a minimal, script-free explanation page (B-6 "Move UA,
don't buy domain"; A-17: the UA names an owned URL, never the operator's personal
identifiers; C-8: no e-mail until `contact@` exists).

- **One contact setting.** `connectors/net.py` `DEFAULT_CONTACT_URL` moves to the
  owned explanation URL (trailing slash, matching the canonical route).
  `connectors/transports/httpx_transport.py` `default_user_agent()` now defaults
  its `homepage` to that constant instead of repeating a literal, and
  `tasks/maproulette.py` builds `SIG-contribution-back` from the same import. The
  historical probe comment in `procurement_portal_tenants.toml` keeps the fact
  (the 2026-09-18 probes ran under the shared UA) without the unowned literal.
- **The page.** `web/src/pages/data-collection.astro` renders through the static
  `BaseLayout` — T0 under ADR-155: no `<script>`, no island, no runtime
  dependency. It states: public records only and no plate/trip/per-person data by
  design; the exact UA form `name/version (+https://surveillancegraph.org/data-collection/)`;
  robots.txt is retrieved, recorded and classified per RFC 9309, and under
  GL-GATE-08 (ADR-088/ADR-168) a `Disallow` or unreachable policy is marked
  `robots_disregarded` rather than silently bypassed; the fail-closed per-source
  rights review is the binding access control; conservative per-host rate limits
  and bounded backoff; and the opt-out route is the dispute channel
  (`/dispute/`). No e-mail appears.
- **Copy discipline.** Every sentence is a sha256-pinned row in the new
  `docs/build/reports/copy-batches/batch-01.md` (the first 11A row needing the
  file creates it), all `pending` — the page ships only once the operator
  confirms the words verbatim (B-2), and P34.17's L2 refuses pending copy. Each
  element's `data-copy` tokens bind it to its rows;
  `tests/unit/test_data_collection_page.py` fails on any drift, uncovered text,
  or hash mismatch.
- **Tests.** `test_net.py` pins the owned constant, the exact UA shape, and the
  absence of `@`/`sig-project.org`, plus a `git grep` scan that fails on any
  `sig-project.org` literal under `connectors/`, `tasks/`, `policy/`, `ops/` and
  `web/src/`; `test_httpx_transport.py` and `test_maproulette_live_transport.py`
  pin the fallback and contribution-back UAs to the shared constant;
  `web/tests/e2e/pages.ts` adds `/data-collection/` to `SHELL_PAGES`, putting the
  built page under the axe sweep, the zero-`<script>` assertion, and the shell
  checks.

## What this does not do

- No robots behaviour changes — GL-GATE-08's probe-record-disregard posture is
  unchanged (the page describes it, it does not set it).
- No `ingestion_permitted` flip, no claim-spine write, no sqitch-plan touch, no
  ADR-body edit, no e-mail or personal identifier added anywhere.
- The stale conduct *prose* (`crawler_conduct.toml` rule 2, the `crawler.py`
  docstring's pre-GL-GATE-08 reading) is untouched — the full conduct text is
  P36.1b's; noted in `runs/P35.38a.md` so the adjacency is recorded, not silent.
- The opt-out register and SIG-INGEST-046c reservation handling stay owed to
  P36.1a; the page claims the route, not a mechanism that does not exist yet.
- Existing connector images keep the old UA until their next roll — the exposure
  B-6 accepted.
